title: Renfe's API changed shape: search-travel leg: missing timestamp (search-new-system)

failed_canaries.what: Madrid-Barcelona on a day Renfe's new system sells, with fares

error.hint: Renfe's web API may have changed; re-capture the request and update renfe/search.py.

acceptance: `renfe search Madrid Barcelona --date 2027-01-29` against the twin in mode shape-drift exits 0 and lists the same trains, times and cheapest fares as against the plain twin: 03000 2027-01-29T06:30:00+01:00 -> 2027-01-29T09:15:00+01:00, cheapest 30.0 EUR; 00600+00500 2027-01-29T07:00:00+01:00 -> 2027-01-29T12:00:00+01:00, cheapest 40.0 EUR; 03100 2027-01-29T09:00:00+01:00 -> 2027-01-29T11:40:00+01:00, cheapest 50.0 EUR; 03200 2027-01-29T13:00:00+01:00 -> 2027-01-29T15:50:00+01:00, cheapest 30.0 EUR
`python -m intake.monitoring --mode shape-drift --check --target <worktree>` exits 0, and so does `--mode plain`
a search-travel leg with neither the old nor the new time fields still stops with exit 7 (api_changed): the parser reads the new shape, it does not silence ApiShapeError
the offline suite passes as it does on the base; tests/fakes.py (the old shape) is not edited
a new test feeds the new shape and fails on the base
the change stays in src/renfe/search.py and tests/; a correct fix exists in about 10 lines of search.py
evidence.new_shape: search-travel legs carry departure_station.departure_timestamp and arrival_station.arrival_timestamp (Madrid local time, ±HHMM, as journey-search writes them) instead of departure_datetime, arrival_datetime and their *_timezone fields
